evidence:
Pairwise review of all 17 scored binary criteria (12 functional, 5 polish), the 5 visual Likert rows and the 2 gates. Most of the design is sound: hro_readonly_roles leaves out request kinds whose staff control never succeeded ('scored only in its own criterion'); hro_messaging, hro_unread_seen and hro_long_thread fall back when candidate conversations or candidate sending fail ('which hro_candidate grades', 'which hro_messaging grades'); functional/prompt.md 'Shared state' tells the judge to judge setup legs against the state the app produced when a feature graded elsewhere (add, single move, re-order, undo) breaks; hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread say arrival speed is 'graded only in Functional'; hro_pol_failed_send defers note drafts to hro_pol_session_resume; hro_intake_restart compares against a before-restart baseline (Colderwater lesson 16 pattern followed); role refusals are split across hro_manager_roles (Ingrid/Bill), hro_readonly_roles (Observer, Tomas writes, anonymous 401), hro_messaging (Ingrid read, Aud/Ingrid/Noor send replays) and hro_candidate (Tomas staff reads, other-application conversation) with no shared observable. No incompatible-product pair found: the 409 stale refusal versus rule-refusal replays is reconciled in functional/prompt.md 'Requests and replays'; the interview-full rollback/focus alternatives in hro_interview_places do not conflict with hro_moves' immediate display; Activity no-line legs only concern refused attempts.

Defect (same observable graded twice, with a contradictory ownership statement): tests/scored/polish/judge.toml hro_pol_live_thread (id line 29, description line 34) grades, when another person's message arrives in the open conversation, that 'the reply still reads exactly what was typed, the box still has focus, and typing more appends to it', then states 'This row owns the draft, the focus and staying at the newest message; where the view goes while reading earlier messages is graded in Functional.' But tests/scored/functional/judge.toml hro_long_thread (id line 107, description line 112, weight 5.5) also grades, when Noor's message arrives in the open conversation, 'the reply still reads exactly what was typed and the box still has focus'. The only difference is scroll position (scrolled up vs at newest); the observable (draft text and composer focus surviving an incoming message in the open conversation) is the same, and the polish row's 'owns the draft, the focus' claim is contradicted. The functional row scores behaviour the polish row says it owns: the cross-dimension double penalty Colderwater lesson 16 warns against. The polish prompt's 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row' only binds within Polish.

Lesser notes (not blocking alone, recorded for reconciliation): (a) hro_moves (weight 7) grades undo of a rejection and of a reopening while hro_undo_activity (weight 7) grades undo generally; the observables differ (reason restoration vs move/multi-move restore and conflict refusal) and hireops_rules.md section 3 'Undo' states both promises, so this is root-cause coupling, not a duplicate observable, but an app without undo loses legs of both. (b) hro_pol_live_board / hro_pol_live_thread score 0 if no live update arrives within 60 s, overlapping the arrival legs of hro_two_people / hro_messaging only for an app with no live updates at all; this is a required positive control (REVIEW_POLICY 'A negative needs a successful control') and the 60 s vs 15 s window confines the overlap, so acceptable. (c) hro_candidate 'each can open and read their own conversations' and hro_messaging step (1) 'as Tomas ... read it and reply' both require Tomas to read his conversation; the messaging fallback covers only a missing new conversation, not a candidate unable to read; minor prerequisite overlap. (d) hro_undo_activity step 9 repeats the blank-reason and skip attempts graded in hro_moves, but only for the 'added no line' Activity leg; 'the refused attempts' wording is adequate.

No configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index scope), so the double penalty is a source defect, not a runtime measurement.
counterexample: An app whose conversation pane re-renders on every incoming message (a common live-update implementation) wipes the composer text and focus in both scroll states. With hro_long_thread's pagination, place-keeping, notice and unread legs all correct, it still fails hro_long_thread (5.5/61 of functional, about 5.4% of total reward) solely for the draft/focus leg, and also fails hro_pol_live_thread (2/9.5 of polish, about 4.2% of total reward) for the same defect, although the polish row states it owns the draft and focus. Conversely, an app that keeps draft and focus when at newest but moves focus to its scrolled-up 'new message' notice passes the row that claims ownership and fails the functional one, so the ownership statement does not match how the task is graded.
suggested_fix: Drop 'the reply still reads exactly what was typed and the box still has focus' from hro_long_thread's bar (keep the unfinished reply only as realistic setup and say draft and focus are graded in Polish hro_pol_live_thread), or move the scrolled-up draft/focus leg into hro_pol_live_thread so its 'owns the draft, the focus' statement is true; then re-review rows 6, 27 and 31 and weights.
